subject: Acme procurement weekly check-in / PO vs card / marketplace interest
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>, procure_ops@acme.com
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-05T15:22:00Z
Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (procurement path)

Hi Sarah / Acme procurement team,

Great to meet yesterday — thanks for the time. Quick recap and suggested next steps so we all have the same view: 

- Need: Reliable, low-latency inference for Acme's customer chat assistant (target start piloting in Q2).
- Preferred deployment: Dedicated capacity or private VPC — final decision depends on legal/PSA review.
- Key procurement questions you raised: PO vs card, acceptance of marketplace purchase, SSO/KMS requirements, and contract term length.

Next steps I proposed on the call:
1) I will send a short SOW + pricing worksheet for your finance team to review (attached).
2) If PO is required, identify the PO contact and expected net terms; we can provide an invoice flow and sample PO language.
3) If marketplace is preferred (e.g., AWS Marketplace), let us know and we'll open that path in parallel — note that marketplace purchase affects billing cadence and support model.
4) Tech follow-up: Dev will do a quick infra checklist to confirm VPC and KMS fit.

Markers for success: signed PO or marketplace purchase + kick-off meeting scheduled.

Attachments: Redwood-SOW-v1.pdf, redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx

Thanks — I'll check back next week for a status update.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0142

From: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: procure_ops@acme.com
Date: 2026-02-09T10:10:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (procurement path)

Thanks Marissa — useful recap. A few follow-ups from procurement ops: 

- Primary question: can we pay by PO with Net 30? If not, we may need to use a company card for the pilot.
- Marketplace: procurement prefers to buy through AWS Marketplace where possible. Does Redwood support that and would feature parity/cost be the same?
- Can you confirm whether we need to sign any additional security addenda (we have a standard DPA + SOC 2 requirement)?

I'll loop in Tim (IT) for the KMS/SSO items if needed. Would appreciate the invoice sample and suggested PO language.

Best,
Sarah
Sarah Jenkins
Sr. Manager, Procurement — Acme Corp

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>, procure_ops@acme.com
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-12T16:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (procurement path)

Hi Sarah — great questions, answers below: 

- PO vs card: We support both. For pilots, many customers use card for speed; for production we can accept PO with Net 30 or Net 45 depending on credit review. I attached a short sample invoice and suggested PO language (see pricing sheet).
- Marketplace: Yes, Redwood is listed on AWS Marketplace. Feature parity is maintained for hosted purchases; dedicated/private options require a separate onboarding flow (we can support via a marketplace purchase + dedicated contract or via direct contract). I'll include the marketplace listing link in the HubSpot record.
- Security addenda: We have a standard DPA and SOC 2 report; if you require a custom addendum we can review it. For KMS/SSO, Dev can confirm technical fit — @Dev, can you confirm the KMS onboarding checklist items?

Attachments: Redwood-SOW-v1.pdf, redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx
Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/123456/company/ACME

If procurement is comfortable with PO + Net 30, we can start contract redlines this week and aim for invoicing in March. If you prefer marketplace, let me know and we'll route through that procurement channel.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-18T09:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Post-call recap + next steps (procurement path)

Hi team — quick infra note:

- KMS: We support customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM for private deployments; for hosted API we can support envelope encryption for data at rest and can plug into Acme's KMS if you opt for private deployment. If acquisition is marketplace-hosted, KMS needs can be handled post-purchase during onboarding.
- Network: If Acme opts for VPC peering or private deployment we'll need a short network checklist (NAT, routing, CIDR ranges).

Happy to jump on a 20-min call with Tim to confirm details.

Dev
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@acme.com>, procure_ops@acme.com
Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai>

Subject: Acme procurement weekly check-in — where is it stuck?

Hi Sarah / procurement ops — weekly check-in: where are we on the decision path? A few specific asks so we can keep momentum: 

1) PO vs card: Can you confirm which payment method procurement prefers for the pilot? If PO, who is the PO contact and expected net terms?
2) Marketplace: Is Acme comfortable buying via AWS Marketplace (we can start that flow in parallel)?
3) Contract redlines: Any redline comments from legal we should prioritize?

If helpful, Vivek and I can host a short sync with procurement and Tim to unblock payment and KMS questions. We've attached the SOW/pricing again for easy reference.

Attachments: Redwood-SOW-v1.pdf, redwood-pricing-sheet.xlsx

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
